title: Meta rolls out new AI tools to detect ads that secretly lead to child sexual abuse material
key_facts: Meta announced on Wednesday (7 Oct 2026) that it took action against 33.2 million pieces of child sexual exploitation content on Facebook and Instagram in the first half of 2026.
More than 97 percent of the content Meta acted on was found by its systems before users reported it; in India it acted on 5.3 million pieces, with more than 98 percent detected first.
A new large language model system detects 'signposting': ads that look normal but may direct users to illegal content or harmful activity elsewhere online.
Meta now looks at where an ad sends users, not only what the ad contains, and can act against the destinations and the accounts behind them.
A 'red-teaming AI agent' tests Meta's own safety measures for weaknesses bad actors could use.
In August Meta agreed to pay up to $18 billion to settle a child safety lawsuit involving 29 US states.
quote_evidence: More than 97% of the content Meta acted on was found by its systems before users reported it, the company said.
Meta said its latest AI tools are aimed at people using ads that look harmless to send users to illegal content outside Meta's platforms.
why_it_matters_hint: Meta is checking where ads lead, not only what they show, to catch ads that point to illegal child abuse material.
notes: Article read in full. Figures and tool claims are Meta's own; no outside review reported in the article.
